name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

prose.intro_html:
Some nights you want dinner to cook itself, and this is about as close as a casserole gets. No boiling a pot of pasta, no browning chicken in batches, no sink full of pans. You blend a creamy sauce, you dump everything into one dish, and the oven does the rest. The dry penne drinks up the chicken broth and the cottage cheese and Boursin sauce while it bakes, so the noodles cook right in the casserole.

Here is why I like it for the wallet and the body both. It leans on chicken breast, cottage cheese, and parmesan for a serious protein load, and it dresses the whole thing up with artichoke hearts, lemon, and a little garlic so it tastes like something you would order out. One batch fills 14 containers at almost 55 grams of protein each, a little over 600 calories a serving, and it does all that without a single fancy ingredient you cannot pronounce.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a one-dish build, so your cart is short and your job is mostly about buying the right sizes.

  • Penne: you need 1 lb 12 oz of dry pasta, which is close to two standard boxes. Any short tube pasta will behave the same way in the oven, so buy whatever short cut is cheapest on the shelf.
  • Chicken breast: grab 3 1/2 lb of boneless skinless breast and cut it into 1-inch cubes yourself. Whole breast almost always beats the pre-cubed tenders on the shelf, and cubing it takes about two minutes.
  • Boursin: the recipe wants 12 oz, which is 2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages. That means you open a third tub and use part of it, so plan on three packages, not two.
  • Cottage cheese: you need 4 2/3 cups, so a large tub. This is the backbone of the sauce, so do not skip it for something lighter.
  • Artichoke hearts and peas: canned artichokes, drained, run about 2 1/3 cans; the peas are frozen, 2 1/3 cups, and go in straight from the bag. Both are pantry and freezer staples you can stock ahead.
  • Lemons and parmesan: two lemons cover both the juice and the zest, and grating your own parmesan off a wedge gives you the 2 1/3 cups you need with better flavor than the shaker can.
prose.make_it:
Start by heating your oven to 400 degrees F and lightly greasing a 9x13 casserole dish. Set it aside while you build the sauce.

Make the creamy sauce in a blender or food processor. Combine the cottage cheese, the crumbled Boursin, the minced garlic, the fresh lemon juice, the lemon zest, and the sea salt, and blend until it is smooth. Then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until everything is completely incorporated. Do not panic when it looks thin, because it is supposed to be very thin. That thin sauce is what the dry pasta is going to soak up.

Now dump and assemble. Spread the dry penne across the bottom of the dish, then scatter the cubed chicken, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over the whole dish and press the pasta down so it is completely submerged. Anything sticking up out of the liquid will dry out, so tuck it under.

Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should be slightly undercooked at this point, which is exactly what you want. Top it with the grated parmesan and slide it back into the oven, uncovered, for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the temperature up if you want the top nice and golden. If the pasta already feels al dente or done, just add the parmesan and move on.

Let the casserole rest for at least 10 minutes after it comes out so it can set up and stop being soupy. Finish with fresh parsley or basil, and serve.
prose.portion_html:
This one is a scoop-and-weigh job. When the casserole comes out and has rested, set your empty container on the scale and zero it out, then weigh the full dish so you know the total. Divide that number by 14 and that is your target weight per container. Portion by weight, not by eyeballing scoops, because a casserole this creamy hides its heavy spots and light spots.

Hit that weight in each of the 14 containers and every one lands at almost 55 grams of protein and a little over 600 calories, with 50.5 grams of carbs and 20.1 grams of fat riding along. Stir a scoop of the parsley or basil across the tops if you portioned before garnishing.

head.description: A no-boil chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, lemon, and a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. Dump and bake in one dish for 14 high-protein meal-prep servings.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, high protein meal prep, artichoke chicken casserole, cottage cheese pasta bake, Boursin chicken pasta, budget meal prep dinner
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish.

In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, and blend until smooth. Add the chicken broth and blend again until fully smooth. The sauce will look very thin, which is correct.

Spread the dry penne across the bottom of the dish, then scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the sauce over everything and press the pasta down so it is completely submerged.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil, stir well, top with the grated parmesan, and return to the oven uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes until the top is golden.
Let the casserole rest for at least 10 minutes, then garnish with fresh parsley or basil and portion into containers.
